source.title: Frequently hypercyclic operators: recent advances and open problems

accepted.question_text: Let X be a separable F-space (for example, a separable Banach space) and T:X→X a continuous linear operator. The Frequent Hypercyclicity Criterion is the standard sufficient criterion asserting that there exist a dense set X0⊂X and a map S:X0→X0 such that, for every x∈X0, the series Σ_{n≥1} T^n x and Σ_{n≥1} S^n x converge unconditionally and TSx=x. Which strong dynamical property, if any, is exactly characterized by this criterion? In particular, if T is chaotic, topologically mixing, and frequently hypercyclic, must T satisfy the Frequent Hypercyclicity Criterion?

evidence.quote:
Problem 1. (a) Which (strong) dynamical behaviour does the Frequent Hyper cyclicity
Criterion characterize?
(b) Does every chaotic, mixing and frequently hypercyclic oper ator satisfy the Frequent
Hypercyclicity Criterion?

accepted.question_text: For a frequently hypercyclic operator T on a Banach space X, let FHC(T) denote the set of frequently hypercyclic vectors, meaning vectors x whose orbit visits every nonempty open set with positive lower density. Can there exist a Banach-space operator T such that every vector of X is the sum of two frequently hypercyclic vectors, i.e. X = FHC(T) + FHC(T)?

evidence.quote:
Problem 2. Is there an operator T on a Banach space X for which X = FHC (T ) +
FHC (T ) holds?

accepted.question_text: Let T be a frequently hypercyclic operator on a Banach or Hilbert space. Must T admit an invariant Borel measure of full support? If X is a Hilbert space, must T admit an ergodic measure of full support? If X is a Hilbert space, must T admit an ergodic Gaussian measure of full support? Finally, if X is a Hilbert space, must T have a unimodular eigenvalue, that is, an eigenvalue λ with |λ|=1? The source notes that the last three questions may also be asked more generally for arbitrary reflexive Banach spaces.

evidence.quote:
Problem 3. (a) Does every frequently hypercyclic operator on an arbitrary Banach space
admit an invariant measure of full support?
(b) Does every frequently hypercyclic operator on a Hilbert spa ce admit an ergodic mea-
sure of full support?
(c) Does every frequently hypercyclic operator on a Hilbert spa ce admit an ergodic Gaus-
sian measure of full support?
(d) Does every frequently hypercyclic operator on a Hilbert spa ce have unimodular eigen-
values?
Questions (b), (c) and (d) may also be asked, more generally, for arbitrary reﬂexive
Banach spaces.

accepted.question_text: Which Banach spaces admit a frequently hypercyclic operator, meaning a continuous linear operator with an orbit that visits every nonempty open set with positive lower density? Which Banach spaces admit a chaotic operator, meaning a hypercyclic operator whose periodic points are dense?

evidence.quote:
Problem 4. Which Banach spaces admit a frequently hypercyclic operato r? Which Banach
spaces admit a chaotic operator?

accepted.question_text: Which compact subsets K of the complex plane can occur as the spectrum σ(T) of a frequently hypercyclic operator T acting on a complex Banach space?

evidence.quote:
Problem 5. Which compact subsets of C can be the spectrum of a frequently hypercyclic
operator on a complex Banach space?

accepted.question_text: If T is a frequently hypercyclic operator on a topological vector space X, can the set FHC(T)∪{0} itself be a linear subspace of X? Here FHC(T) is the set of frequently hypercyclic vectors of T.

evidence.quote:
Problem 6. Can the set FHC (T ) ∪ { 0} be a linear subspace of X if T is frequently
hypercyclic?

accepted.question_text: A frequently hypercyclic subspace for an operator T is an infinite-dimensional closed subspace all of whose nonzero vectors are frequently hypercyclic for T. Characterize the weighted backward shifts B_w on ℓ^p, 1≤p<∞, that possess a frequently hypercyclic subspace. More generally, characterize the operators on separable complex Banach spaces that possess a frequently hypercyclic subspace.

evidence.quote:
Problem 7 (Menet). (a) Characterize the weighted backward shifts Bw on ℓp, 1 ≤ p< ∞ ,
that possess a frequently hypercyclic subspace.
(b) More generally, characterize the operators on a separable ( complex) Banach space
that possess a frequently hypercyclic subspace.

accepted.question_text: Must every chaotic operator be frequently hypercyclic? Here a chaotic operator is a hypercyclic operator with dense periodic points, whereas a frequently hypercyclic operator has some orbit that visits every nonempty open set with positive lower density.

evidence.quote:
Problem (Bayart-Grivaux). Is every chaotic operator frequently hypercyclic?
This problem has since been iterated in various articles, an d it has come to be considered
as one of the major questions in linear dynamics; see, for exa mple, [8, Chapter 6] and [43,
Chapter 9]. Menet [47] very recently obtained a counter-exa mple.
Theorem 15 (Menet). There exists a chaotic operator that is not frequently hyper cyclic.

accepted.question_text: Do there exist Banach spaces that support a chaotic operator but no frequently hypercyclic operator, or Banach spaces that support a frequently hypercyclic operator but no chaotic operator?

evidence.quote:
Problem 8 (Menet). Are there Banach spaces that support a chaotic operator but n o
frequently hypercyclic operator, or vice versa?

accepted.question_text: If T is an invertible frequently hypercyclic operator, must the inverse operator T^{-1} also be frequently hypercyclic?

evidence.quote:
Problem 9. IfT is an invertible frequently hypercyclic operator, is then a lsoT − 1 frequently
hypercyclic?

accepted.question_text: If T is a frequently hypercyclic operator, must the direct sum operator T⊕T also be frequently hypercyclic?

evidence.quote:
Problem 10. If T is a frequently hypercyclic operator, is then also T ⊕ T frequently
hypercyclic?
